mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the CPIAUCSL inflation index above 3% in a month triggers a preemptive equity risk premium, as investors anticipate future rate hikes and discount future cash flows more heavily, driving positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 3.0 in a single month
failure_condition: Over a 12-month window, 20-day forward returns do not outperform a 5-day rolling average during the same inflation surprise episode (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in PAYEMS labor cost growth exceeding 0.5% monthly for two consecutive months signals wage stickiness, prompting equity market anticipation of higher labor costs and corporate profit pressures, which elevates S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by more than 0.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: During such labor cost trends, 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than during a neutral labor cost regime (rolling mean difference p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous surge in both HOUST retail sales and GDPC1 personal consumption, each above 2% month-over-month, indicates robust consumer and business demand, which elevates equity valuations and drives positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 2.0% MoM AND GDPC1 > 2.0% MoM in the same month
failure_condition: During such double-digit demand acceleration, 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than during single-digit growth periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in INDPRO manufacturing index (decline > 5%) coincides with a rise in RSAFS inventory drawdowns, signaling tight supply conditions that compress production lags and boost near-term equity risk premia, producing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by more than 5% in a month AND RSAFS rises in the same month
failure_condition: During supply shocks, 20-day forward returns do not show statistically significant deviation from a baseline neutral supply shock window (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 4.00% for three consecutive months in a non-recessionary regime, it indicates persistent monetary easing, which lowers real discount rates and supports higher equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 4.00% for three consecutive months AND macro regime is non-recessionary
failure_condition: Over a 12-month low-rate window, 60-day forward returns are not higher than during a comparable high-rate window (rolling mean difference p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in UNRATE unemployment rate below 4.0% for two consecutive months in a labor market cooling phase is interpreted as a tightening labor supply, which increases wage growth expectations and elevates equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4.0% for two consecutive months AND labor market cooling regime
failure_condition: During such UNRATE declines, 20-day forward returns do not outperform during a neutral unemployment rate window (rolling mean difference p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: When a sharp drop in GDPC1 personal consumption (decline > 3%) occurs without a corresponding rise in HOUST retail sales, it signals demand weakness that outweighs supply-side easing, depressing equity valuations and producing negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls by more than 3% in a month AND HOUST does not rise by more than 1% in the same month
failure_condition: During such events, 5-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during baseline demand expansion (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden, unanticipated spike in FEDFUNDS above 5.25% in a non-inflationary context creates a one-time discount rate shock that sharply compresses the present value of future equity cash flows, producing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS jumps above 5.25% in a single month AND inflation is below 3.0% that month
regime_hint: transitory high-rate surprise in low-inflation context
failure_condition: During such spikes, 20-day forward returns do not show significant negative deviation from a pre-spike baseline (rolling mean difference p > 0.10).
